title: Bonami's hypercontractivity lemma for low-degree functions
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function whose Fourier expansion has degree at most $k$; that is, every nonzero Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is supported on a set $S$ with $\abs{S} \le k$. When $\{0,1\}^n$ is equipped with the uniform probability measure, $f$ is $9^k$-reasonable: its fourth moment is controlled by the square of its second moment via
\[
\E[f^4] \le 9^k \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2 .
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on {0,1}^n
f has degree at most k (nonzero Fourier coefficients supported on sets of size at most k)
the uniform probability measure is used on the hypercube
replaced:
A Boolean function $f$ of degree at most $k$ is $9^{k}$-reasonable under the uniform measure on
the hypercube.
